forecasts.label: Capital expenditure

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Waverley reports £2.9m General Fund and £3.0m housing account underspends for 2025/26
news_drafts.lead:
Waverley Borough Council ended 2025/26 with a £2.9m underspend on its General Fund, the account that pays for services funded by council tax and business rates. Its housing revenue account, the ring-fenced account for council housing paid for by rents, underspent by £3.0m. The figures are in the annual report of the council's external auditor, which went to the Audit & Risk Committee on 16 November 2026.

The General Fund underspend compares with £1.7m in 2024/25, and the housing account's with £1.02m. The General Fund result includes £2.4m of staffing savings and £1.7m of treasury income.

The auditor's report says: "While the General Fund and HRA outturn positions were favourable, these were influenced by non-recurring factors rather than the delivery of recurring savings." It says both results were driven by non-recurring factors.

news_drafts.headline: Waverley opened 2026/27 with a £7.3m general fund deficit, forecast to narrow to £4.5m by year-end
news_drafts.lead:
Waverley Borough Council began the 2026/27 financial year with its main day-to-day account (the general fund) £7.3m in deficit, and forecasts it will end the year £4.5m in deficit, according to budget papers for its Executive committee on 6 October. The council puts the £2.8m improvement down to £1.1m of budget movements and £1.7m from commitments, money already set aside for specific purposes.

The papers show a similar pattern in the money set aside against business rates, the tax on commercial property. The reserve for timing differences on government grants and for spreading the cost of a deficit started the year £3.75m in deficit. Budget movements of £2.67m are forecast to bring that to £1.08m in deficit. A separate reserve covering risks to the council's medium-term financial plan, its multi-year forecast of spending against income, is forecast at minus £665k, after £197k of budget movements and £280k of commitments.

Two income lines are forecast below budget. Planning land charges, the fees for property searches, are expected to bring in £345,565 against a budget of £406,070, a shortfall of £60,505 or 14.9%. Commercial Waverley Training Services is forecast at £368,965 against £406,635, a shortfall of £37,670 or 8.5%.

findings.headline: Commercial Services external-organisation debt totals £1,214,967, the largest service line in that category.
findings.detail: The external organisations table lists Commercial Services at £1,214,967 in total, with £839,450 in the first band and £325,552 in a later band. The paper does not say what the debt relates to, so the cause is not known from this document.
findings.matters: A large single-service debtor balance from external organisations is a concentration risk, and finance officers at other councils would want to know what drives it.
findings.figures: Commercial Services external total £1,214,967; first band £839,450; another band £325,552

findings.headline: Business Rates Collection Fund debt is £23,401,482, with a Collection Fund bad debt provision of £2.1m.
findings.detail: The footnote says the total is the whole collection fund debt, of which Waverley's share is 40%. The £2.1m provision is set aside to be written off against the debt and is said to mitigate any impact on the general fund.
findings.matters: A finance director would compare the size of the bad debt provision to the outstanding balance, and peers would compare how provisions are set against collection fund debt.
findings.figures: Business Rates Collection Fund debt £23,401,482; bad debt provision £2.1m; Waverley share 40%

findings.headline: Council Tax Collection Fund debt is shown as £71,226,717, with a Council Tax impairment provision of £11,357,000.
findings.detail: The footnote says the Council Tax figure is total collection fund debt and that the impairment provision will mitigate any impact on the general fund. The paper gives a Waverley share of about 12% (£1,463,669), but this does not reconcile with the total, so the share figure should be read with care.
findings.matters: The size of the impairment provision against collection fund debt determines how much of any non-collection falls on the general fund, which matters to finance directors and to lenders assessing the council's reserves.
findings.figures: Council Tax Collection Fund debt £71,226,717; Council Tax impairment provision £11,357,000; WBC share £1,368,488 (2025-6); WBC share ~12% (£1,463,669)
findings.quote: We have a total Council Tax Collection Fund impairment provision of £11,357,000

findings.headline: Housing - GF service-user debt totals £627,023, with £427,482 in the over-365-days column.
findings.detail: Housing - GF is the largest service-user debt line in the table. Housing - HRA service-user debt is £325,906, with £148,793 in the over-365-days column. The column allocation is inferred from the row and column totals, because the table's blank cells are not labelled.
findings.matters: Aged housing debt from service users is a recovery and collectability question that finance officers at other councils with temporary accommodation or rent arrears will compare directly.
findings.figures: Housing - GF total £627,023, over 365 days £427,482 (inferred); Housing - HRA total £325,906, over 365 days £148,793 (inferred)

findings.headline: Total debt of £3,354,985 at Quarter 2 2026/27, of which £1,109,795 has been outstanding for more than 365 days.
findings.detail: The Total Debt row shows £1,509,173 in the 0-90 day band and £1,109,795 over 365 days. The over-365-day balance is made up of £508,192 from external organisations, £581,487 from service users/fee payers and £20,116 from public sector organisations.
findings.matters: A finance director, or a peer council comparing its own aged debt, would want to know how much of the sundry debtor book is over a year old and where it sits.
findings.figures: Total debt £3,354,985; 0-90 days £1,509,173; 90-180 days £159,330; 180-365 days £577,661; over 365 days £1,109,795; external over 365 days £508,192; service users over 365 days £581,487; public sector over 365 days £20,116

daily_post.headline: The planned works team is using an interim planned works surveyor appointed via agency for 3 months to cover capacity challenges.
daily_post.lead: Interim cover and reorganisation-linked procurement delays are pressures other councils and their finance teams may be managing at the same time.
